classification.difficultyReason: Use each prescribed scale and the supplied quadruple-angle identity, then select four distinct cosine values and rescale them to polynomial roots.

content.prompt: Solve the following. You may assume the identity $\cos4\theta=8\cos^4\theta-8\cos^2\theta+1$.

answer.worked:
Let $x=2\cos\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}16\cos^4\theta-16\cos^2\theta+2&=0\\2(8\cos^4\theta-8\cos^2\theta+1)&=0\\2\cos4\theta&=0\\\cos4\theta&=0.\end{align*}$$
For $0\le\theta\le\pi$,
$$\begin{align*}4\theta&=\frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{3\pi}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{2},\ \frac{7\pi}{2}\\\theta&=\frac{\pi}{8},\ \frac{3\pi}{8},\ \frac{5\pi}{8},\ \frac{7\pi}{8}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$x=2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right),\quad2\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{8}\right),\quad2\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{8}\right),\quad2\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{8}\right).$$
These four distinct roots exhaust the roots of the quartic.

Let $x=\sqrt2\cos\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}8\cos^4\theta-8\cos^2\theta+1&=0\\\cos4\theta&=0.\end{align*}$$
For $0\le\theta\le\pi$,
$$\begin{align*}4\theta&=\frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{3\pi}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{2},\ \frac{7\pi}{2}\\\theta&=\frac{\pi}{8},\ \frac{3\pi}{8},\ \frac{5\pi}{8},\ \frac{7\pi}{8}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$x=\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right),\quad\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{8}\right),\quad\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{8}\right),\quad\sqrt2\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{8}\right).$$
These four distinct roots exhaust the roots of the quartic.
